title: Nexus weekly roadmap crib - Rafael
content:
Purpose:
- Quick prep notes for the Monday cross-team check. Keep short, focus on blockers that need decisions from product + eng + applied-ml.

Context / TL;DR:
- Two parallel rollouts next sprint: hosted-api model upgrade (v2.1 -> v2.2-quant) and a Dedicated capacity perf tweak (batcher v3).
- Research has an eval showing small hallucination increase on a subset of prompts after quantization; infra telemetry shows tail-latency improvement but a few spikes on 512+ token flows.
- Product wants clear gating criteria: customer-facing quality floor + latency SLOs.

Agenda (10–20 min):
1) Quick status from each: Product (product goals for sprint), Eng (canary plan, infra risk), Research (eval summary + unresolved concerns). 3 min each.
2) Decide rollback/fallback policy for v2.2-quant (soft vs strict).
3) Latency SLO trade-offs: what to accept for 95th vs 99th in exchange for 20% cost savings.
4) Action item assign + owners for canary run and prompt set watchlist.

Key notes to bring up (short bullets):
- Research: small but measurable drift on open-domain QA prompt set A (precision down ~2.8%). Need to verify if prompt engineering mitigates.
- Eng: batcher v3 reduces average token latency by ~18% on p3dn, but a 0.4% increase in infra retry rate when KV cache misses coincide with large batches. Might be config/timeout tuning.
- Product: prioritize top-3 enterprise customers (Acct A,B,C) — we should offer a short FTR (feature-toggle) window if they see regressions.
- Ops: watch memory pressure on 40k-context tests; add one more max-worker for the canary pool.

Unresolved questions for the meeting:
- Is 2.8% precision drop acceptable if we can rollback per-route fast? (Product decision)
- Do we require a hard quality gate (no measurable metric regression on curated prompts) or soft (human-in-the-loop monitoring + rollback window)?
- Can Eng reduce batcher burst size to mitigate KV miss retry spike without losing latency gains?

Short experiment notes (for Research):
- Re-run eval w/ temperature tuned to 0.0/0.2 on the problematic prompt cluster tomorrow morning.
- Try prompt anchor (prefix) experiment: does a 1–2 token anchor reduce hallucination? quick A/B with 500 samples.

Decisions we should try to get in this call:
- Canary plan: 1% traffic -> 5% over 24h -> 20% over 48–72h with automated rollback if precision drops >1.5% on watchlist. (vote: product + research + eng)
- Fallback route: route enterprise customers to v2.1 (non-quant) automatically if they hit quality regression for two consecutive checks.
- Latency SLO: keep 95th <= 220ms and allow 99th <= 520ms for burst windows during canary (temp relaxation). If exceeded more than 3 times in 6h, pause rollout.

Action items (clear, short):
- AI-1: Research (Maya) -> Re-run narrowed eval + prompt-anchor A/B by EOD 2026-04-30. Deliver quick table of precision/recall deltas.
- AI-2: Eng (Sanjay) -> Prepare canary infra: one extra worker in canary pool, configure auto-rollback hooks (thresholds above). Due 2026-05-01 AM.
- AI-3: Product (Leah) -> Draft enterprise comms + feature toggle plan for Acct A/B/C; add support oncall schedule. Due 2026-05-01 EOD.
- AI-4: Ops (Rafael) -> Add telemetry dashboard widget for prompt-watchlist, include quick links to eval results and to the rollback toggle. Due 2026-05-02.

Follow-ups + reminders to self:
- Bring up cost impact numbers during decision: show per-token cost delta and projected monthly $ savings at 20/50/100k QPS. (quick table)
- If Research's A/B shows anchor reduces hallucinations by >1.2% without hurting latency, prefer soft-gate + staggered increase.
- Confirm oncall overlap for the 72h window (we need weekend coverage if rollout hits Fri).

Notes-to-self (brain-dump):
- Keep meeting <25 min. If heavy debate, schedule a focused 30m "quality gating" deep-dive with extended slate of prompts.
- Keep the watchlist: 1) open-domain QA A, 2) summarization-edge B, 3) code-completion C. Short IDs and owners next to each.
- Avoid committing to full Dedicated capacity change until canary passes on hosted first.

Quick links to paste in meeting chat:
- Confluence plan: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/rdw-roadmap-2026
- Canary ticket: JIRA-RDW-4123
- PR for batcher change: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/2146

End of crib. Short, direct, flag the decision points early in the call.
